what: Cheniere Energy liquefies natural gas and ships it abroad. It owns the Sabine Pass and Corpus Christi terminals in Texas and Louisiana, the largest liquefied natural gas export capacity in the United States.
customers: Utilities and energy companies in Europe and Asia under long-term contracts, plus buyers in the spot market.
money: long-term contracted cargoes plus spot sales
moat: Export terminals that cost tens of billions and take years to permit and build, with capacity sold out under twenty-year contracts.
risks: Debt of about $27 billion was raised to build the terminals
Spot gas prices swing and affect the uncontracted portion of volumes
Permitting and policy decisions can delay expansion projects
A mild winter in Europe or Asia reduces demand for extra cargoes
opportunities: Most capacity is contracted for twenty years with fixed fees paid whether or not gas is lifted
European buyers want supply that does not come from Russia
Expansion trains at both terminals add capacity through the decade
watch: Volumes shipped and the share of revenue under fixed-fee contracts.
